results.content:
A journey map is a point-in-time artifact. It captures what users experience during the period covered by the research. But if you are doing this work repeatedly, across multiple projects, multiple products, multiple user types, you are accumulating something more valuable than a collection of maps. You are accumulating a searchable, comparable record of how user experiences change over time, which pain points persist, which ones get solved, and which ones come back under different names. [...] The intake skill takes the synthesis and confirms what the map needs to be: one persona (always one per map), the specific scenario being mapped, where the journey starts and ends, what type of map this is, and which industry stage library to use. SaaS maps have a different default stage structure than AEC maps or Film/TV production maps. The skill knows this and asks one question at a time rather than dumping a form. [...] — -

## If You Want to Build This

I am not open-sourcing the skill files yet, but I am happy to talk through the architecture with anyone working on similar problems. The design decisions that matter most are the source tagging system, the schema-first data model that drives all rendering, and the critique layer that prevents generic output from leaving the pipeline.

Three months of research. Four weeks of translation. With the agent, those four weeks compress to a session. The thinking is still yours. The agent handles the collation.

Reach out here or find me on LinkedIn.

# Android Studio adds 'agentic AI' with Journeys feature, Agent Mode

Sarah Perez

3 min read

 GOOG

  -1.37%

Android Studio, the integrated development environment (IDE) for Android app developers, is getting an AI upgrade, Google announced at its developer conference, Google I/O 2025, on Tuesday.

In addition to the rollout of the latest Gemini 2.5 Pro model, Android Studio is gaining a new "agentic AI" capability called Journeys and will soon introduce an "Agent Mode" for more complex development tasks.

Using Gemini, journeys will allow developers to test their app by describing the actions and assertions in natural language for the user journeys across the app. Gemini will then perform the tests for you.
